thread:
samir: Heads-up — noticed a customer report where streaming responses + mid-stream tool_call triggered a retry and the token accounting jumped. Looks like tokens for the in-flight stream chunk + tool_call were counted twice.

jess: Ugh. Do we have logs for that session? Is it client retry or server-triggered re-send? :thinking:

samir: Server retried because we didn't ack the streaming websocket frame due to a transient NACK. The client reconnected and re-requested the same stream with the same conversation id, but our metering code counted the partial tokens from before the reconnect and then again after recovery.

kai: Can you paste the meter trace? I want to see how we tag streaming fragments vs completed responses.

samir: Pasting snippet from metering-bot:
```
metering-bot: session=cs_9f8a, chunk_id=81b, tool_call=translate_en, tokens_before=124, tokens_after=310, billed=186
metering-bot: session=cs_9f8a, chunk_id=81b, tokens_replayed=124, billed=124 (no dedupe)
```

olivia: That looks like we incremented billed both on initial chunk and on replay. We should be deduping by (session, chunk_id) but tool_call boundaries might have reset internal ids.

jess: Are tool_calls creating a new sub-request id that makes chunk dedupe fail? I remember a PR where tool_call transitioned to a synchronizing state and cleared chunk mappings.

samir: Exactly — when a tool_call starts mid-stream we create a tool_transaction_id and attach it to subsequent chunks. If a reconnect happens we re-emit the earlier chunk without the tool_transaction_id (race), so dedupe key mismatches.

kai: Two immediate mitigation options:
- Preserve stable chunk ids across tool_call boundary (better but invasive)
- Add a replay detection layer in metering that dedupes by chunk content hash + session id for recent windows

olivia: From a product/console perspective customers are seeing quota dips that don't match usage. Dashboards show spikes that correspond to these replay events. We need a telemetry event to mark replay vs fresh billing so support can filter.

jess: Agreed on telemetry. Minimal fix: add a "replay=true" metric when we detect a reconnect and suppress billing increment. Longer term: ensure stable ids.

samir: Also FYI tool calls sometimes include truncated prompt snippets in logs which affects content-hash dedupe. If truncation happens before we compute the hash we might end up with different hashes for same logical chunk.

kai: Good point. For hashing solution we must hash canonicalized token sequence (post-truncation rules) and compute at the earliest emit point.

olivia: UX/Rollout ask: When we deploy fix, we should surface a console banner for affected customers explaining "quota drift" and that we'll retroactively credit duplicates for a 48h window. Also add a per-route toggle to enable the strict dedupe mode so power users can opt-in earlier.

samir: I'll open a short RFC. Proposed tasks:
1) telemetry event + support filters — owner: olivia — 48h
2) server-side replay suppression (replay flag) — owner: jess — patch in next deploy
3) canonical chunk id + stable ids across tool calls — owner: kai — design spike this week
4) retro credits script — owner: samir — follow-up after dedupe

metering-bot: note: created metering-issue #873 with labels [billing, streaming, toolcall]

olivia: Thanks. I'll draft customer banner + console toggle copy and loop legal for credits language.

jess: I'll do a quick patch to add replay suppression and flag in the metering event schema. PR when ready.

kai: Spike will include a small benchmark: hashing overhead per chunk and collision risk. If cheap, we can roll hashing + cache.

samir: Thanks team. If anyone sees a different replay example (esp with truncation + tool_call) drop it here. I'll add a test case that simulates websocket NACK + mid-stream toolcall.

olivia: Adding a note for rollout UX: add a metric to the rollout dashboard indicating dedupe hits/misses so SRE can watch for regressions.

jess: +1. We'll also add an alert if billing delta > 5% for a customer in 1h window.

samir: OK closing for now. Will post the RFC link here when created.
